title: For Blended and Co-Parenting Families
description: Kinrows has no custody-record feature. What it doesn't do, what a shared calendar across two homes helps with, and when to use a dedicated co-parenting tool instead.
directAnswer: Kinrows is not a custody-record or legal-communication tool — it has no court-admissible logging, expense-reimbursement tracking, or documented-communication feature the way OurFamilyWizard, TalkingParents or 2houses do, and if a custody arrangement requires that kind of record, one of those purpose-built tools is the right choice. For co-parents on cooperative terms who mainly need a shared calendar and lists visible across two homes without merging every other part of family life, Kinrows' household and clan structure can help.
keyTakeaway: Cooperative co-parenting and court-monitored custody are different problems, and Kinrows only fits one of them.

sections.heading: What a dedicated co-parenting app does that Kinrows doesn't
sections.html:
Apps built specifically for custody arrangements — OurFamilyWizard, TalkingParents, 2houses, KidCal, Pairently, Kidtime — exist because some co-parenting situations need a documented, sometimes court-admissible record: logged messages, expense-reimbursement tracking, and calendars built around custody-day tracking designed to hold up if things get contentious. One category leader's own positioning is that it "handles complex custody schedules that other family calendar apps can't manage" — a real, specific capability, and not one Kinrows has.

Kinrows has no custody-record feature, no court-admissible message log, and no legal-communication tool. If a custody order requires documented communication, or a mediator or court has recommended a specific app, use that app for that purpose.

sections.heading: Where a shared calendar across two homes still helps
sections.html: For co-parents coordinating cooperatively — not adversarially — a shared household calendar with two-way phone sync means school events, appointments and pickups show up on both parents' phones without one person re-typing what the other already entered. Recurring events and per-person color coding help when a kid's schedule is split across two homes with different routines.

sections.heading: Keeping each home's other data (budget, notes) separate
sections.html: A household in Kinrows is a private inner circle — budgets, private notes and the full calendar live there and aren't visible outside it. Two co-parenting households don't need to merge into one household to share a calendar; each can keep its own household for its own home's data, while a separate Clan (an unlimited, invite-code group) is where the things that genuinely need to be shared across both homes, like a kid's milestones or a shared events calendar, actually live.

sections.heading: When to use a court-recommended co-parenting app instead
sections.html: If a custody arrangement is contentious, court-monitored, or requires a documented paper trail of communication and expenses, a purpose-built tool designed for exactly that is the right call, not a general household organizer. Kinrows is built for the logistics of running a home, not for the legal and evidentiary needs of a custody dispute, and being honest about that distinction is more useful than implying otherwise.

productFit.heading: A shared calendar without merging everything else
productFit.html: Two-way sync with each parent's own phone calendar means events entered on either side show up for both, without asking either parent to give up their existing calendar habits. Per-person color coding helps distinguish which parent's home a given event belongs to at a glance. This covers the shared-schedule part of co-parenting logistics; it is not a substitute for a custody-record or legal-communication tool where one is needed.

faq.q: Is Kinrows good for co-parenting or custody schedules?
faq.a: It depends on what kind of co-parenting. Kinrows has no custody-record, court-admissible logging, or legal-communication feature, so it isn't a substitute for OurFamilyWizard, TalkingParents or similar tools where a custody arrangement requires that. For cooperative co-parents who mainly need a shared calendar and lists across two homes, Kinrows' household and clan structure can help.

faq.q: What's the difference between Kinrows and a dedicated co-parenting app?
faq.a: Dedicated co-parenting apps are built around documented, sometimes court-admissible communication and custody-day tracking designed to hold up if a situation becomes contentious. Kinrows is a general household organizer — a shared calendar, lists, chores and budget — with no custody-specific record-keeping at all. A household in an adversarial custody situation should use the purpose-built tool.

faq.q: Can two households share a calendar without merging everything else?
faq.a: Yes. A Clan is a separate, unlimited group joined by invite code that overlaps with a household only through the people added to it, so two co-parenting households can share a calendar or updates through a clan while each keeps its own household's budget and private notes to itself.
